name: profile-close-window-light
prompt: Photorealistic vertical close-up portrait, framed from the top of the shoulders to just above the crown, made on an 85mm lens at f/1.8 so only the wool is sharp. A masked figure is turned three-quarters, the left side of their head toward the camera, chin lifted and throat stretched as they stare up at something enormous above them. The whole head is covered by a charcoal balaclava of chunky cable-knit yarn, its face a smooth, unbroken expanse of wool, no holes cut anywhere for sight, breath or speech. A thick band of white yarn is sewn in a full circle around the face. Within that circle, set high in its upper-right arc as the viewer sees it, directly over where the left eye would be, sits a small red felt triangle with softened corners, plainly off to one side, never central. The lower edge of the knit disappears inside the raised corduroy collar of an olive waxed cotton jacket, and a black knitted glove holds the collar closed, the sleeve cuff covering the wrist so no skin shows at all. A low late-afternoon sun pours through an unseen window on the left, a warm honey-coloured shaft that rakes across the wool, lighting every loop and loose fibre and leaving the far cheek in soft brown shadow. Behind and above the figure, dissolved into creamy blur, a towering wall of stacked paper reams and bundled documents fills the top half of the frame in cool bluish white; one sheet near the figure's line of sight shows a bold black printed heading, THE RULES, readable through the softness. Palette of warm amber and charcoal against cold paper white, fine film grain, an everyday room in present-day Britain, only cloth and paper, nothing shiny, metallic or lit up.
